newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shrug off Nikkei's tumble.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs shrug off Nikkei's tumble.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures gave up most of their initial gains in late Thursday trade despite huge losses on the Tokyo stock market for the third straight day.
Growing economic worries pushed the 225-share Nikkei average down 606.51 points or 3.25 percent to 18,073.87 at the close. The index has lost 1,287.48 points in the first four trading days of 1997.
"There is huge concern over the stock market's performance. And there's now talk of liquidation of bonds to cover losses in stocks," said a Japanese bank dealer.

He said Euroyen futures showed limited upside potential and a strong stock market rebound on Friday could push September Euroyen down towards 99.10. The contract was quoted unchanged from its IMM close of 99.29 at 1125 GMT.
March JGBs settled at 124.84 against their previous 124.76, after hitting a high of 125.25.
Eurodollar futures ended little changed after coming under slight pressure on growing expectations of a bullish U.S. employment report for December on Friday.
"Quite a number of houses are expecting a higher (non-farm payrolls) number. The bonds have been quite nervous today," said the dealer.
He said SIMEX players had been unable to push June Eurodollars through support at 94.17, but this level could give way during trade in Chicago, exposing the contract to further declines.
"After that, there's not much support nearby so it would give a good opportunity to go short," he added.
The contract ended unchanged from its IMM close, at 94.19. Turnover was at 9,501 lots. -- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
